subject: biology
title: Human Physiology Adventure 3: Hormones, neurons and homeostasis
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet neurons and the endocrine messengers that hold you in balance.
meta_desc: Biology — neuron action potential, synaptic transmission, hormones, insulin/glucagon, ADH.
final_note: You learned action potentials use Na⁺/K⁺ channels, synapses use neurotransmitters, and homeostasis relies on negative feedback by hormones.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Resting: -70 mV (Na⁺/K⁺ pump + leaky K⁺ channels).

Threshold ≈ -55 mV opens voltage-gated Na⁺ channels → depolarisation to +30 mV.

K⁺ channels open → repolarisation → brief hyperpolarisation.

Myelin speeds conduction via saltatory propagation between nodes of Ranvier.

Action potential opens Ca²⁺ channels in presynaptic terminal → vesicles release neurotransmitter (e.g. acetylcholine).

It diffuses across the cleft (~20 nm), binds receptors → ligand-gated channels open → postsynaptic potential.

Cholinesterase clears ACh. Cocaine blocks dopamine reuptake; many drugs target synapses.

Insulin (β cells, islets of Langerhans): glucose↑ → insulin↑ → uptake by liver/muscle → glycogen storage.

Glucagon (α cells): glucose↓ → glucagon↑ → glycogen breakdown.

ADH (posterior pituitary): blood [solute]↑ → ADH↑ → aquaporins added to collecting duct → water reabsorbed.

Type 1 diabetes: autoimmune β cell loss. Type 2: insulin resistance — rising globally with obesity.
